title: Eval signal harmonizer + on-call suppression adapter for Console routing
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: Evals-generated quality regression signals are currently noisy when multiple config/model changes happen in a short window. PMs and on-call engineers receive many near-duplicate Slack/PagerDuty notices (same underlying regression surfaced by multiple evals or model variants), which increases alert fatigue and slows root-cause attribution.

Goal: Build a Console-side "signal harmonizer" that groups related eval regressions by change provenance (model/config diff, rollout id, user cohort), computes an impact score, and emits consolidated notifications to Slack and PagerDuty. Add an "on-call suppression adapter" that recognizes planned rollouts and applies adaptive suppression windows or sticky grouping rules to avoid noisy pages during deployment storms.

Scope: Console routing + alerting config, server-side grouping algorithm, PagerDuty dedup key conventions, Slack thread + channel formatting, new provenance fields on eval events, and a small UX surface in Console to view grouped incidents and their contributing evals. This ticket covers the product definition, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and follow-ups with Eng/Design/Support for implementation and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Console receives eval events with provenance tags (model-id, config-diff-id, rollout-id, customer-segment)
Signal harmonizer groups >= 90% of near-duplicate regressions from the same change into a single consolidated notification (measured on last 30 days of historical eval events)
Slack: consolidated messages post to a single channel with a thread containing expanded contributing evals and direct links to eval dashboard rows
PagerDuty: consolidated pages use a deterministic dedup_key based on grouping hash so only one incident is created per grouped failure; pages still include a link to grouped eval details
On-call suppression adapter honors scheduled rollouts (Console rollout API) to apply configurable suppression windows and exposes reason in the grouped notification
Console UI shows a grouped incident view that lists contributing evals, impact score, first-seen timestamp, and suggested owner
Telemetry: reduce duplicate incident creation by at least 60% in pilot orgs and decrease time-to-action (TTD) for grouped incidents by >=20%
Documentation: runbook and Console docs updated with examples for configuring suppression settings and troubleshooting grouped alerts
design_notes: Design proposal favors a lightweight grouping heuristic initially: 1) require provenance overlap (same rollout-id OR model-id+config-diff within 15 minutes) and 2) impact-weighted scoring (metric delta * affected-traffic estimate) to choose lead eval. UX wires include a compact grouped card in Notifications with an expandable thread showing contributing evals and 'silence for rollout' button. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Signal+Harmonizer+Design
implementation_plan: API: add provenance fields to eval event schema (model_id, config_diff_id, rollout_id, affected_pct)
Backend: build grouping service in Console that consumes eval event stream, applies grouping heuristic and computes impact score
Alerting: implement PagerDuty dedup_key strategy (grouping-hash:v1) and Slack thread poster that tags subscribers
UI: grouped incident view + settings panel to tune suppression windows per project
Testing: run historical backfill sim to measure grouping precision/recall and pilot with 3 internal teams
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout with opt-in at org level, monitor metrics, then enable-by-default after 4-week pilot
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: over-aggressive grouping could hide distinct regressions — Mitigation: include configurable similarity threshold and show contributing evals prominently
Risk: missed pages during high-severity regressions if suppressed — Mitigation: severity override: any eval with severity>=critical bypasses suppression
Risk: PagerDuty compatibility across customers with different routing rules — Mitigation: expose dedup_key policy and allow orgs to opt-out of dedupe and use tags instead
metrics: Duplicate incident reduction (%): target >=60% for pilot orgs
False grouping rate (% of groups that contained unrelated regressions): target <=10%
Mean time to detect (MTTD) for grouped incidents: improve by >=20%
PagerDuty pages suppressed per rollout: track counts and reason codes
Slack threads created per day: expected to drop while thread depth may increase
